summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute viral gastroenteritis causing severe diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, which exacerbated her chronic pancreatitis and gastroparesis. Over nine days, her symptoms resolved with conservative management including IV fluids, low-dose narcotics, and gradual resumption of tube feeds up to 50 cc/hr. Her type 1 diabetes was stabilized with adjusted insulin dosing, and psychiatric symptoms remained controlled on her baseline regimen. Stool studies ruled out bacterial pathogens. Pain management was transitioned from IV Dilaudid to oral hydromorphone for discharge, with tramadol discontinued due to patient refusal during admission. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume her prior insulin regimen, continue tube feeds, and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
